message: Running command: cd /workspace/repo-vul/src-vul/gpac && grep -rn "GF_M4ASampleRates" src/ include/ | head -30

message.content:
Now I understand the vulnerability. The issue is that `GF_M4ASampleRates[ctx->acfg.base_sr_index]` is accessed with an out-of-bounds index. The `base_sr_index` comes from the LATM audio config parsed from the input. If `base_sr_index` is too large (>= the size of the `GF_M4ASampleRates` array), then `GF_M4ASampleRates[ctx->acfg.base_sr_index]` reads out of bounds (heap-buffer-overflow READ of 9 bytes - since each element is likely 4 bytes... wait, READ of 9 bytes).

Actually, the fix checks `if (!GF_M4ASampleRates[ctx->acfg.base_sr_index])`. But the real issue is that `base_sr_index` can be out of bounds of the array. Let me look at `GF_M4ASampleRates` and `gf_m4a_parse_config`.

Let me look at the avparse code.
